newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Syria message exchange eased tensions - Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Syria message exchange eased tensions - Netanyahu.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday Israel had received messages from Syria via third parties saying it had no aggressive intentions against the Jewish state.

Netanyahu referred to clarifications sent by Israel to Damacus via the United States, Russia and France that the Jewish state had no aggressive intentions and return messages to Israel from Syria via the third parties to the same effect.
"With the Syrian clarifications a Syrian commitment was created. That has importance," Netanyahu said.
He said tensions that had soared between the two arch foes lessened in the wake of the exchange.
"Can this thing bring the opening of talks? Certainly," Netanyahu added.
On Monday, Syrian President Hafez al-Assad told a news conference in Damascus that he could not rule out an Israeli attack on Syria or Lebanon.
Tensions between Israel and Syria have been running high since Netanyahu took office in June.
Syrian troop movements in Lebanon last month and a series of military exercises have given Israel war jitters. Damascus has said the redeployment was defensive.

More than five years of painstakingly slow peace talks between the two countries have stalled over the Golan Heights captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal. Netanyahu has vowed never to give up the strategic plateau.
The peace talks have been suspended for eight months since a wave of suicide attacks by Islamic militants killed 59 in the Jewish state.
